brief: Nordea expects two more Fed hikes and two more 25bp ECB hikes (December, March 2027), with risks to both skewed toward faster tightening. The Fed case rests on inflation unlikely to ease: the Iran conflict is pushing oil prices up, already visible in diesel and jet fuel costs, with fertilizer-driven food price pressure still to come; AI-linked investment and equity-driven wealth gains are supporting demand; and the labor market is tightening, evidenced by upward payroll revisions, a 162,000 August print against a ~55,000 consensus, and Warsh calling the economy near full employment. The Fed's own year-end dot now implies another hike. For the ECB, market pricing already sits above Nordea's baseline; the September meeting revised inflation forecasts higher, with core above target through 2028, but showed no urgency beyond the existing quarterly pace, though an escalating Middle East conflict and rising gas prices tilt risk toward an October move. Nordea separately maintains its long-standing call for higher longer-term yields, flagging a near-term correction risk given aggressive short-end pricing.
